items.title: Eddie Summers Interview, 1963-11-11
items.q: Well, uh, he's teaching me about music

ctx.x: I'd pick up the air and the jazz, you know. Who was it taught you to play? I mean, or did you just pick it up and play and improvise and jazz? It taught me? Yeah. Well, I almost learned, you can learn yourself how to play by air and by head, you know. Yeah, I guess. I mean, but why did you choose to play that kind of music? If, you know, if Vic was teaching you music, how come you didn't stand with music? You just...

Well, uh, he's teaching me about music, but, uh, I see that wasn't, that wasn't a go at that time, was it, Harry? That wasn't a go at that time. The music was okay, but he wanted some of that, uh, rough stuff. Yeah. How much did he charge for lessons? Do you remember that? Well, he used to charge me cheaper. He'd charge me a dollar quarter. That was for an hour, or what? No, a dollar quarter for about two hours. We was kind of friends, like. Yeah. We was friends, like. Uh-huh. How much did he charge everybody? I…

I guess lessons were pretty cheap in those days. Lessons were cheap anyway, though, you know? Well, I mean, I have it one charge dollar, dollar, dollar. Yeah. Professor Shining, but the other one around to charge the ball. Quiet. Yeah. And he'd give you a lesson to him. Yeah. I'm telling you. Let me think, uh, where did we get to, uh, in the 40s, uh, what, what, uh, so you just went back with, uh, Sheik's band when you came back here from California?
